factchecks.title: Fact check: Fakes spread online amid Syria's power shift
factchecks.verdict_label: DW Fact check: Fake   There are two major issues with this claim.    The first is that the video is AI-generated. This can be seen, for example, in the inconsistencies in the sandbags in the background that warp and flicker. In addition, her tears disappear or land unnaturally on her T-shirt. Also, the soldier’s name tag reads "WHADR," a nonexistent surname, and the lettering visibly trembles.   HIVE Moderation, an AI detection tool, assessed the clip as 69% likely AI-generated. The TikTok handle which appears in the video links to an accountthat only posts short videos of female soldiers with similar nametag issues.    The second hint is in the caption. The soldier does not use the quoted words, "shame and embarrassment," nor does she mention anything about the United States’ involvement in the region.    The US was once the SDF's main ally. But after negotiations fell apart, the US shifted its support to the new government.
factchecks.explanation:
"An American female soldier stated that she feels 'shame and embarrassment' regarding the events in Rojava, affirming that the United States has indirectly contributed to the commission of crimes against Kurdish fighters."

This is the caption for a videoof a woman in army garb, crying and wiping her tears in front of a waving American flag. In the video, she says, "I just wanted to let you know that I’m doing well. It’s been such a tough journey, but I’ve been trying my best to hold on for all of us."

factchecks.verdict_label: DW Fact check: True. Posts on Xand TikTokclaiming that thousands of New York Police Department (NYPD) officers had resigned following Mamdani's victory, or that trucking companies were suspending operations in the city, were falseor satire, but this one is true.   NYFD Commissioner Robert Tuckerhanded in his resignationone day after Mamdani's election. The timing was unusual as the commissioner typically waitsfor a successor to be named before resigning.   Tucker himself stated in an interview with the Israeli newspaper The Jerusalem Postthat he holds different opinions than the newly elected mayor, citing ideological misalignment.   "I also think I could have functioned well under him but, ideologically, our feelings are different. Therefore, I think he deserves the respect of appointing his own commissioner, someone who may be more aligned with him ideologically than I am."
factchecks.explanation: NYC Fire Chief resigns over mayoral election

factchecks.verdict_label: DW Fact check: Misleading  Some users in the commentsinterpret the image as being taken after the current ceasefire went into effect. That is not what this is. A reverse image search reveals that the photo is actually a still from a longer video. It is circulating with similar claims, for instance in Russian, stating: "As soon as there is a ceasefire, Gaza is full of pumped-up, armed men in military uniform".    These posts suggest the footage is from the latest ceasefire, but the video is old and unrelated to current events. A 17-second video was already postedon January 26, 2025. Back then, the people in Gaza were celebrating the peace deal that was in effect from January 19 to March 18, 2025.
factchecks.explanation: "Hamas is the only army in the world that wears civilian clothes during war and puts on uniforms during ceasefires", an X user wrote, sharinga picture allegedly showing the uniformed Hamas fighters during celebration of the recent ceasefire in Gaza.

factchecks.claim: A post on X featuring a video allegedly showing recent lootings in South Africa, and captured: "This is Durban, South Africa," is currently going viral. The post was published by Alex Jones, a US-based far-right radio host known for promoting conspiracy theories. He claims: "This is what removing 'White Oppression' and replacing it with Soros NGO systems looks like. A glimpse into the future of ALL Western countries if changes are not made fast as already seen in the SH!T HOLE blue city's [sic] across America." The post had 1.6 million views at the time of publication.
factchecks.title: Fact check: Viral Durban video misrepresents South Africa
factchecks.verdict_label: DW Fact check: Misleading   The video posted on X does not show a recent situation in Durban, a city in the east of South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal province. While the footage does show a shopping street in central Durban, as the geolocation of the scene indicates,  it was not recorded recently. A reverse image search by DW Fact check revealed that the video had already circulated on X and Facebook in 2021. Comparisons with official agency photos from that time confirm that the footage dates back to July 2021. The video captures a moment during a period of unrest in South Africa, when parts of the country were engulfed in riots and widespread looting  — sparked by the imprisonment of former President Jacob Zuma. He had been sentenced to 15 months in prison for failing to comply with a Constitutional Court order to testify before a commission investigating corruption during his presidency. His arrest triggered protests, particularly in his home province of KwaZulu-Natal, which includes Durban — the city featured in the video.  Zuma's supporters viewed his arrest as unjust and rallied to demand his release, criticizing the judiciary. However, Zuma's imprisonment was only one of several triggers for the unrest. Underlying causes included economic hardship, high youth unemployment, political disillusionment with the African National Congress (ANC), and opportunistic criminal activity. The riots ultimately left more than 300 people dead.  Since 2021, the video has resurfaced repeatedly across various social media platforms and in multiple languages. A similar claim using the same footage went viral again in March of this year.  Dhanaraj Thakur, a researcher at the Center for Democracy and Technology, sees this as part of a broader strategy, "a larger campaign with many different actors sharing similar kinds of messages," he told DW. "Some of these actors have an intent to create misunderstanding and promote this kind of racist narrative."
factchecks.explanation: A post on X featuring a video allegedly showing recent lootings in South Africa, and captured: "This is Durban, South Africa," is currently going viral. The post was published by Alex Jones, a US-based far-right radio host known for promoting conspiracy theories. He claims: "This is what removing 'White Oppression' and replacing it with Soros NGO systems looks like. A glimpse into the future of ALL Western countries if changes are not made fast as already seen in the SH!T HOLE blue city's [sic] across America." The post had 1.6 million views at the time of publication.

factchecks.claim: Claim: In a TikTok postwith over 800,000 views, a woman says, "They're throwing the deportees out of the planes and into the ocean. [...] they're shackling people, flying out into open ocean and throwing them out. The flight patterns, there is people tracking them on this app, the flights going out with the deportees. Watching them go out to the open ocean and circle back. A family in Italy saw five shackled bodies wash up on the shore." These claims have surgedon social media repeatedly in the past days.
factchecks.title: Fact check: Viral ICE deportation claims debunked
factchecks.verdict_label: DW Fact check: Unproven   While ICE does shackledeportees on flights during air operations, there has been no evidence to support the claim that people have been thrown out of planes.  Starting with the statement on the flight patterns, it is possible to track live air traffic through services like Flightradar. However, no publicly available app specifically tracks the deportations in real time.  The non-profit organization Witness at the Bordermonitors US policies on its borders and has tracked US deportation flights electronically since the COVID pandemic by using publicly available online databases.   Immigration activist Tom Cartwrightwrites regular reports on where and how often  deportation flights take place, which have become invaluable sources for major news outletssince ICE does not regularly provide such data. Some have called him the "go-to source for information about ICE flights" or "the leading expert in the field."   Asking about flight tracking data being used to support the claim that deportees are being thrown from ICE flights into the ocean, Cartwright told DW: "These videos have no basis in fact. I have tracked over 40,000 ICE Air flights over 5 1/2 years and never have I seen anything that would even in a remote way support any of these spurious claims."   We also did not find recent news stories of shackled bodies washing up on the shores of Italy. factchecks.claim: Scientists have had to pause the Climate Change Hoax Scam
factchecks.title: Fact check: Climate deniers misinterpret Antarctic ice study
factchecks.verdict_label: Misleading: One post even featured a GIF that the user believed showed new land emerging off the coast of Dubai due to falling sea levels — apparently unaware of the artificial Palm Islands constructed there between 2001 and 2007. The findings in the Chinese study are based on publicly available data from NASA's Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment satellites, which have been measuring the Earth's gravitational field since 2002 and have documented changes in the planet's ice and water masses. The data may be correct, but its interpretation by conspiratorial social media users is not — a situation not helped by the researchers' decision to insert an increasing average trend curve next to the preceding decreasing curve depicting ice mass.  "This is perfect fodder for people who are intentionally looking to spread disinformation," said Johannes Feldmann, a physicist at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research near Berlin.  Feldmann emphasized that climate science relies on long-term data — typically over 20 to 30 years — to identify meaningful trends. "Two, three or even five years are far too little to identify a long-term trend," he explained.  Cherry-picking short-term data is a common tactic among climate change deniers. "There are always phases where the increase [in temperature] levels off a bit, which people suddenly take to mean: global warming has stopped, the trend is reversing," Feldmann added. "But it's never turned out to be true."
factchecks.explanation: Scientists have had to pause the Climate Change Hoax Scam

factchecks.claim: NATO has allegedly deceived and disrespected Russia by expanding into Eastern Europe, threatening Moscow's interests. That, at least, is how the Kremlin has justified its war in Ukraine. But is there any truth to it?
factchecks.title: Did NATO expansion drive Russia to war?
factchecks.verdict_label: NATO leaders have gathered in The Hague in the Netherlands on June 24 and 25 to discuss the topic of increased defense spending, and support for Ukraine will be high on the the agenda.  Russia's invasion of Ukraine is now well into its fourth year. As the fighting drags on, the United States has increasingly demanded that its NATO allies shoulder a greater share of the costs of funding the alliance, whose members have been providing significant military and financial support to Kyiv.  In the past four years, NATO has been a target of false narratives time and again. DW Fact Check looked at some of the most common claims.   However, for the Russian President Vladimir Putin, NATO itself represents a threat to Russian national security — especially since its post-Cold War expansion into Eastern Europe, which includes countries that had formerly been part of the Soviet Union or at least in the Soviet sphere of influence.  The prospect of Ukraine, a country with even stronger historical and cultural ties to Russia, drawing closer to or even joining NATO — or indeed the European Union — has been cited by Putin as justification for Russian interference in Ukraine since 2014 and the so-called "special military operation" launched in February 2022.  As early as March 2000, speaking to the BBC in one of his first interviews as Russian president, Putin insisted that he was not opposed to NATO but stressed concerns about the alliance's eastward expansion, which by that point had already seen Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic join as members.
factchecks.explanation: NATO has allegedly deceived and disrespected Russia by expanding into Eastern Europe, threatening Moscow's interests. That, at least, is how the Kremlin has justified its war in Ukraine. But is there any truth to it?

Other versions of the same video have appeared across platforms like X and YouTube, reaching millions of users in different languages.
factchecks.title: Fact check: Viral US Iran strikes videos are fake or old
factchecks.verdict_label: Fake  The video is generated with artificial intelligence, and has no connection to the actual US strike on nuclear sites in Iran.   The earliest known source of the clip is a social media account that clearly states in its description that all of its content is AI-generated. A reverse image search of key frames shows the footage appeared online several days before the operation, with some posts then falsely claiming it depicted an Iranian missile strike on Israel.  There are multiple visual indicators that the video is not authentic. The glow from the explosion, for instance, fails to cast realistic light or reflections on nearby buildings or smoke. The urban layout features Soviet-style buildings, which are uncharacteristic of Iranian cities. Moreover, none of Iran's nuclear facilities targeted in the strike are located near large urban centers like the one depicted here.
factchecks.explanation: US missile hits Iran," wrote one TikTok user on a video that shows a massive explosion near or inside a city, with a mushroom-shaped cloud of smoke rising into the sky. Other versions of the same video have appeared across platforms like X and YouTube, reaching millions of users in different languages.

factchecks.claim: Claim: Wind energy is "a con" and not truly green, as wind turbines aren't properly recycled, this social media user said in a post on X, sharing a photo of a bulldozer burying what looks to be parts of windmills.
factchecks.title: Fact check: Debunking Trump's false claims on wind energy
factchecks.verdict_label: DW Fact check: Misleading  The photo is real and was published 2020 in a Bloomberg report showing wind turbines in the ground at the Casper Regional Landfill in Wyoming. It's also available on the stock photo service Getty Images. There are other sites of such wind turbine graveyards in the US, for instance in Iowa and South Dakota, where wind turbine blades are chopped up and buried.  At the moment, about 90% of the mass of a decommissioned wind turbine can be recycled, according to the US Department of Energy.Some renewable energy companies say they recycle up to 95% and have committed to stop sending turbine blades to landfill.  Germany, Austria, Finland and the Netherlands already have a landfill ban in place. And the European wind industry, represented by WindEurope, is calling for a Europe-wide landfill ban on decommissioned wind turbine blades by 2025.  Steel towers, concrete foundations and copper cables are relatively easy to recycle, according to the Fraunhofer Institute for Wind Energy Systems (IWES) — but since rotor blades are made of different materials, recycling these parts was much more complex.  Even though some of the blades are being repurposed and used as playground equipment, bicycle shelters or material for skis, "the usual disposal method is currently thermal recycling of the shredded rotor blades in the cement industry," Fraunhofer said.  Next-generation rotor blades are recyclable with a new type of resin that allows for the separation of composite materials so they can be reused.
factchecks.explanation: Claim: Wind energy is "a con" and not truly green, as wind turbines aren't properly recycled, this social media user said in a post on X, sharing a photo of a bulldozer burying what looks to be parts of windmills.

factchecks.claim:
Claim: "These are the -- these are burial sites right here," Trump said (White House videominute 24:25), while describing a footage during a meeting with Ramaphosa at the White House on May 21.

"Each one of those white things you see is a cross. And there's approximately a thousand of them. They're all white farmers, the family of white farmers," added Trump.
factchecks.title: Fact check: Trump's South Africa 'genocide' claim is wrong
factchecks.verdict_label: DW Fact check: False Trump's claim was already circulating on social media before Ramaphosa's state visit to the US. On May 12, a user on X explained that every cross stands for a murdered white farmer in South Africa. The video posthas been viewed almost 55 million times at the time of publishing.  A reverse image search shows that the footage used by Trump with the white crosses on the side of the road was already shared on social media in 2020 and 2023. These are not, as Trump claims, the gravesites of more than a thousand murdered farmers. Instead, the scenes show a protest near the South African city of Newcastle on September 5, 2020. The protest was triggered by the murder of married couple Glen and Vida Rafferty on their farm in August 2020.
factchecks.explanation:
Claim: "These are the -- these are burial sites right here," Trump said (White House videominute 24:25), while describing a footage during a meeting with Ramaphosa at the White House on May 21.

"Each one of those white things you see is a cross. And there's approximately a thousand of them. They're all white farmers, the family of white farmers," added Trump.

factchecks.claim: "The European Commission plans to take €10 trillion of citizens' savings for EU defense. This is economic suicide. *Get your money out of European banks. They're going to take your money from your bank account."
factchecks.title: Fact check: Does the EU want to 'steal' private savings?
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The controversy and heated discussions on social networks were sparked by two EU initiatives. First, the European Commission presented the White Paper for European Defence – Readiness 2030, which aims to enable member states to invest more rapidly and significantly in their defense sectors. Second, the Commission introduced its strategy for a savings and investment union. This strategy is designed to create more incentives for investment, allowing Europe-wide funds to be established, making it easier for citizens to invest their money in various sectors, including environmental, digital technology and defense. But this doesn't mean the EU has access to private savings accounts. It's not possible based on the current legal system. On the contrary, a number EU regulations are designed to protect citizens' savings.
factchecks.explanation: "The European Commission plans to take €10 trillion of citizens' savings for EU defense. This is economic suicide. *Get your money out of European banks. They're going to take your money from your bank account."

factchecks.verdict_label: Trans women — who were assigned to the male sex at birth but identify as female — have male advantages. If they undergo hormone therapy as part of gender-affirming measures, the differences to cisgender women are reduced. But even then, there are still advantages. Expert opinions differ on the extent to which fair competition between trans and cis female athletes is possible. The male advantage also plays a different role depending on the sport. While it creates major differences in strength sports, such as weightlifting, the situation is different in shooting or dance sports. Last but not least, the issue of fairness must also be weighed against that of inclusion. But experts agree on one thing: There is a great need for further studies on the athletic performance of trans people in elite sports.
factchecks.explanation: Do trans women have unfair athletic advantage in female competitions?

factchecks.explanation: The Australian government enables health practitioners to vaccinate patients under sedation without their knowledge.

factchecks.title: Pfizer vaccine claim misleads on efficacy measures
factchecks.verdict_label: Misleading. The two percentages relate to different measures of efficacy. Experts say the 95 per cent figure is more relevant in gauging real-world effectiveness.
factchecks.explanation: The Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine was only ever 0.86 per cent effective - not 95 per cent as claimed by the pharmaceutical company.

factchecks.title: Facts the best medicine for error-strewn Japanese vaccine meme
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Japanese children are vaccinated from two months and the country has consistently high inoculation rates.
factchecks.explanation: No child under the age of two is vaccinated in Japan.

factchecks.claim: A report shows COVID-19 vaccines had a rate of injury 50 times higher than other vaccines.
factchecks.title: Senator's vaccine report calculations don't add up
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The report contains numbers of suspected adverse events following vaccination, not vaccine-induced injuries, and the 50 times greater calculation is incorrect.
factchecks.explanation: A report shows COVID-19 vaccines had a rate of injury 50 times higher than other vaccines.

factchecks.claim: The US medicine regulator breached its own guidelines by failing to test the mRNA COVID-19 vaccine for DNA integration.
factchecks.title: No, regulator did not breach vaccine testing guidelines
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The guidelines refer to DNA vaccines, not mRNA vaccines.
factchecks.explanation: The US medicine regulator breached its own guidelines by failing to test the mRNA COVID-19 vaccine for DNA integration.

factchecks.claim: A biologist has revealed the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine contains 200 billion pieces of dangerous DNA.
factchecks.title: Senate hearing used to propel vaccine DNA fears
factchecks.verdict_label: Misleading. The biologist said any risk of harm is theoretical and untested. Health agencies have said there is no evidence that any DNA in the vaccine causes harm.
factchecks.explanation: A biologist has revealed the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine contains 200 billion pieces of dangerous DNA.

factchecks.claim: Mercury in flu vaccines causes Alzheimer's and exacerbates symptoms of people who have the disease.
factchecks.title: Facts put flu vaccine mercury claim to bed
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Flu vaccines in Australia and New Zealand do not contain mercury. Regardless, no link has been found between mercury in vaccines and Alzheimer’s disease.
factchecks.explanation: Mercury in flu vaccines causes Alzheimer's and exacerbates symptoms of people who have the disease.

factchecks.claim: New Zealand health data shows COVID vaccines have caused excess deaths.
factchecks.title: NZ data does not show spike in vaccine-related deaths
factchecks.verdict_label: False. COVID vaccines have not caused excess deaths in New Zealand.
factchecks.explanation: New Zealand health data shows COVID vaccines have caused excess deaths.

factchecks.claim: MPs were the only public servants in New Zealand not to be subject to COVID-19 vaccine mandates.
factchecks.title: Vaccine mandate falsehoods injected into NZ election
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Only public servants in high-risk and public-facing roles were subject to vaccine mandates.
factchecks.explanation: MPs were the only public servants in New Zealand not to be subject to COVID-19 vaccine mandates.

factchecks.claim: The New Zealand government is considering putting COVID-19 vaccines into city water supplies.
factchecks.title: Truth sold down the river in post about COVID vaccine in NZ water
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The story is a fabrication and the original Facebook post is a fake.
factchecks.explanation: The New Zealand government is considering putting COVID-19 vaccines into city water supplies.

factchecks.claim: There were more than 1,200 vaccine-related deaths in the first 90 days of the Pfizer rollout.
factchecks.title: Anti-vaxxers misrepresent Pfizer report to say 1200 died in the first ...
factchecks.verdict_label: False: The claim that the deaths were caused by the vaccine misrepresents what the published data on adverse events actually means.
factchecks.explanation: There were more than 1,200 vaccine-related deaths in the first 90 days of the Pfizer rollout.

factchecks.claim: Employers can be jailed under the “Corporate Manslaughter Act” for adverse vaccine reactions suffered by their employees.
factchecks.title: Confused vaccine manslaughter claim based on non-existent law
factchecks.verdict_label: False. There is no such Act and experts say such cases would not apply under existing industrial manslaughter legislation.
factchecks.explanation: Employers can be jailed under the “Corporate Manslaughter Act” for adverse vaccine reactions suffered by their employees.

factchecks.claim: The Moderna COVID-19 vaccine has been withdrawn from Australia
factchecks.title: Moderna vaccine claim gets a jab of truth
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Moderna’s bivalent booster and paediatric dose vaccine are widely available across the country.
factchecks.explanation: The Moderna COVID-19 vaccine has been withdrawn from Australia

factchecks.claim: Pfizer has added a new ingredient to its COVID-19 vaccine to reduce the risk of children having heart attacks as a side effect.
factchecks.title: Child health concerns didn't prompt new Pfizer vaccine ingredient
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The ingredient has been added for greater flexibility in storage and is unrelated to any side effects.
factchecks.explanation: Pfizer has added a new ingredient to its COVID-19 vaccine to reduce the risk of children having heart attacks as a side effect.

factchecks.claim: Official data has confirmed 800 COVID-19 'vaccine deaths' in Australia.
factchecks.title: No, COVID vaccines have not killed 800 in Australia
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The claim is based on a misrepresentation of vaccine safety data. Only 11 deaths have been causally linked to COVID vaccines in Australia.
factchecks.explanation: Official data has confirmed 800 COVID-19 'vaccine deaths' in Australia.

factchecks.claim: A scientific paper shows COVID-19 mRNA vaccines cause five times more cases of myocarditis than the virus itself.
factchecks.title: Myocarditis study misrepresented to fuel vaccine claim
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The claim comes from a misreading of the study. The paper does not - and cannot - show excess risk following COVID vaccination versus COVID infection.
factchecks.explanation: A scientific paper shows COVID-19 mRNA vaccines cause five times more cases of myocarditis than the virus itself.

factchecks.claim: A university study shows that the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine enters the nucleus of a human cell.
factchecks.title: A Swedish study did not say COVID vaccine changes human DNA
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The study authors said this was not the finding of their work, which examined if mRNA from the vaccine could be changed into DNA in liver cancer cells.
factchecks.explanation: A university study shows that the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine enters the nucleus of a human cell.

factchecks.claim: More than 1500 athletes have suffered cardiac arrest since COVID vaccinations began, compared to a previous average of 29 per year.
factchecks.title: Pelé's death linked to vaccine in 'ridiculous' COVID claim
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The claim is based on a list that attributes deaths to cardiac arrest even when another cause is known, such as cancer or car accidents.
factchecks.explanation: More than 1500 athletes have suffered cardiac arrest since COVID vaccinations began, compared to a previous average of 29 per year.

factchecks.claim: COVID-19 data from England suggests that vaccinated people have a higher risk of dying with the virus than the unvaccinated.
factchecks.title: England COVID deaths data misused in false vaccine efficacy claim
factchecks.verdict_label: False. A fair analysis of the data shows unvaccinated people are far more likely to die with COVID-19 across all age groups.
factchecks.explanation: COVID-19 data from England suggests that vaccinated people have a higher risk of dying with the virus than the unvaccinated.

factchecks.claim: Whooping cough vaccines do not work and have never been tested for safety.
factchecks.title: Doctor's vaccine claim fails to cough up the truth
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The vaccines have high efficacy rates and have been deemed safe following extensive testing.
factchecks.explanation: Whooping cough vaccines do not work and have never been tested for safety.

factchecks.claim: Eighty per cent of pregnant women in NZ who have been vaccinated for COVID-19 experience miscarriages.
factchecks.title: No, most vaccinated pregnant women in NZ haven't miscarried
factchecks.verdict_label: False. There is no evidence of increased rates of miscarriage among vaccinated pregnant women in NZ or elsewhere.
factchecks.explanation: Eighty per cent of pregnant women in NZ who have been vaccinated for COVID-19 experience miscarriages.

factchecks.claim: Australia approved a pharmaceutical company to vaccinate its citizens aerially via so-called chemtrails.
factchecks.title: Chemtrails vaccine claim is a flight of fancy
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The approval was for an orally ingested cholera vaccine trial. Vaccines can't be effectively sprayed from an aeroplane.
factchecks.explanation: Australia approved a pharmaceutical company to vaccinate its citizens aerially via so-called chemtrails.

factchecks.claim: You can sue doctors if they can't prove a 'side effect' following the COVID-19 vaccine was not caused by the jab.
factchecks.title: Claim doctors can be sued over COVID vaccines lacks legal standing
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The medical profession bears no burden of proof against claims of negligence under Australian laws.
factchecks.explanation: You can sue doctors if they can't prove a 'side effect' following the COVID-19 vaccine was not caused by the jab.

factchecks.claim: The Gardasil HPV vaccine can cause ovary damage.
factchecks.title: No evidence of link between vaccine and ovary damage
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Multiple studies show there is no link between the vaccine and ovary damage.
factchecks.explanation: The Gardasil HPV vaccine can cause ovary damage.

factchecks.claim: COVID-19 vaccines accelerate coronary artery disease.
factchecks.title: Doctor spins theory to blame Warne's death on COVID vaccines
factchecks.verdict_label: False. There is no evidence to support the claim.
factchecks.explanation: COVID-19 vaccines accelerate coronary artery disease.

factchecks.claim: COVID-19 vaccines cause infertility.
factchecks.title: Vaccine link to infertility barren of any evidence
factchecks.verdict_label: False. There is no scientific evidence that COVID vaccines harm the fertility of women or men.
factchecks.explanation: COVID-19 vaccines cause infertility.

factchecks.claim: England has banned COVID vaccines for pregnant women and children aged under five.
factchecks.title: UK vaccination bans claim is heavy with misinformation
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The UK government advises pregnant women to get vaccinated. COVID vaccination has not been offered for UK children aged under five.
factchecks.explanation: England has banned COVID vaccines for pregnant women and children aged under five.

factchecks.claim: New Zealand Police is considering an inquiry into deaths linked to COVID-19 vaccinations.
factchecks.title: No, NZ Police is not launching a probe into vaccine deaths
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Police say they have no plans to investigate alleged COVID-19 vaccine deaths.
factchecks.explanation: New Zealand Police is considering an inquiry into deaths linked to COVID-19 vaccinations.

factchecks.claim: Data reveals tens of thousands of deaths in New Zealand are linked to COVID-19 vaccines.
factchecks.title: NZ vaccine deaths claim lacks any evidence
factchecks.verdict_label: False. NZ health authorities say four deaths have been linked to the vaccines.
factchecks.explanation: Data reveals tens of thousands of deaths in New Zealand are linked to COVID-19 vaccines.

factchecks.claim: COVID-19 vaccines are more deadly than the COVID virus.
factchecks.title: Fatally flawed research underpins senator's vaccine tweet
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The research underpinning the claim is flawed. Death rates for vaccinated people are no higher than for unvaccinated people.
factchecks.explanation: COVID-19 vaccines are more deadly than the COVID virus.

factchecks.claim: Antarctic sea ice extent is 17 per cent higher today compared to 1979.
factchecks.title: Climate 'lies' claim misrepresents Antarctic sea ice loss
factchecks.verdict_label: Misleading. The claim cherry-picks dates and ignores long-term trends.
factchecks.explanation: Antarctic sea ice extent is 17 per cent higher today compared to 1979.

factchecks.claim: Rising CO2 and temperatures are behind the global boost in grain production over the last 60 years.
factchecks.title: Grain production graph misleads on climate change impact
factchecks.verdict_label: Misleading. Research reveals the increase in grain production is despite the combined impact of CO2 and temperatures, not because of it.
factchecks.explanation: Rising CO2 and temperatures are behind the global boost in grain production over the last 60 years.

factchecks.claim: The World Economic Forum (WEF) has ordered governments to arrest people who deny climate change is happening.
factchecks.title: Climate change deniers not at risk of WEF arrest
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The person said to have made the statement is not associated with the WEF, and he did not say climate change deniers should be arrested.
factchecks.explanation: The World Economic Forum (WEF) has ordered governments to arrest people who deny climate change is happening.

factchecks.claim: The leading cause of climate change is a cosmic influence occurring every 12,000 years.
factchecks.title: Cataclysmic 'cosmic cycle' is kooky climate conspiracy
factchecks.verdict_label: False. There is no evidence of a 12,000-year geological cycle which affects climate change.
factchecks.explanation: The leading cause of climate change is a cosmic influence occurring every 12,000 years.

factchecks.claim: The Climate Council has received $41 billion in funding from the Australian government.
factchecks.title: Climate funding claim way off the money
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The Climate Council does not receive government funding. Its annual revenue is about $8 million.
factchecks.explanation: The Climate Council has received $41 billion in funding from the Australian government.

factchecks.claim: The term global warming was changed to climate change because the earth wasn’t warming as predicted.
factchecks.title: Mish-mash of misinformation gives climate change a bad name
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Global warming is still used to describe a warming planet and was never interchangeable with climate change. The earth has warmed, as predicted.
factchecks.explanation: The term global warming was changed to climate change because the earth wasn’t warming as predicted.

factchecks.claim: Earth hasn’t warmed since the mid-1980s and has only warmed by 0.7C since the 1850s.
factchecks.title: Global temperature data leaves climate sceptic out in the cold
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Global temperatures have increased by around 1.1C since the industrial revolution, with the greatest rate of change occurring in recent decades.
factchecks.explanation: Earth hasn’t warmed since the mid-1980s and has only warmed by 0.7C since the 1850s.

factchecks.claim: The second law of thermodynamics shows man-made global warming is impossible.
factchecks.title: Climate sceptics on wrong side of thermodynamics law
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The greenhouse effect is consistent with the second law of thermodynamics.
factchecks.explanation: The second law of thermodynamics shows man-made global warming is impossible.

factchecks.claim: There is no evidence carbon dioxide directly causes any change in the climate.
factchecks.title: Senator blowing hot air with climate science denial
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Numerous scientific bodies and studies have found an increase in CO2 in the atmosphere has changed the climate.
factchecks.explanation: There is no evidence carbon dioxide directly causes any change in the climate.

factchecks.claim: The Morrison government cut climate spending by 35 per cent in the 2022 federal budget.
factchecks.title: Did the budget include a 35 per cent cut to climate spending?
factchecks.verdict_label: Mostly True. Budget papers show a 35 per cent decline in funding for climate programs over four years, although this doesn't necessarily account for all spending by government agencies.
factchecks.explanation: The Morrison government cut climate spending by 35 per cent in the 2022 federal budget.

factchecks.claim: US billionaire George Soros attended the UN’s COP26 climate summit in 2021.
factchecks.title: Soros climate summit conspiracy a case of mistaken identity
factchecks.verdict_label: False. George Soros was not on the participant list at COP26. The claim appears to have mistaken Sir David Attenborough for Mr Soros.
factchecks.explanation: US billionaire George Soros attended the UN’s COP26 climate summit in 2021.

factchecks.claim: The planet has been in a period of global cooling since 2015.
factchecks.title: Scientists roast climate denier on cooling claim
factchecks.verdict_label: Misleading. The claim relies on cherry-picked data, selecting a particularly hot year as the base. Longer-term data shows a clear trend of rising global temperatures.
factchecks.explanation: The planet has been in a period of global cooling since 2015.

factchecks.claim: Temperatures in Australia have cooled over the last 100 years.
factchecks.title: Climate claim BOMs in attempt to rewrite temperature history
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Australia has been warming since national temperature records began in 1910.
factchecks.explanation: Temperatures in Australia have cooled over the last 100 years.

factchecks.claim: Recent global warming is comparable with natural rates of climate change over the past 10,000 years.
factchecks.title: Climate 'facts' post is a meltdown of misinformation
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Experts say the rate of warming is without comparison and is set to increase.
factchecks.explanation: Recent global warming is comparable with natural rates of climate change over the past 10,000 years.

factchecks.claim: A graph proves humans are responsible for only around 3.5 per cent of the increase in atmospheric CO2 from 1870 to 2020.
factchecks.title: Climate sceptic muddles his maths with emissions claim
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The author has mistaken the graph’s annual emissions figure for the cumulative total since 1870. Humans are responsible for 100 per cent of the increase.
factchecks.explanation: A graph proves humans are responsible for only around 3.5 per cent of the increase in atmospheric CO2 from 1870 to 2020.

factchecks.claim: Scientists have never proved that human emissions of carbon dioxide drive global warming.
factchecks.title: Geologist misleads with climate change 'proof' claim
factchecks.verdict_label: Misleading. Proof does not exist in science but experts say the evidence puts the theory beyond any reasonable doubt.
factchecks.explanation: Scientists have never proved that human emissions of carbon dioxide drive global warming.

factchecks.claim: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has committed Australian taxpayers to $2 trillion per year in climate change payments.
factchecks.title: $2 trillion climate fund claim a red hot lie
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Australia has indicated support for an international climate “loss and damage” fund but has not yet committed any money.
factchecks.explanation: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has committed Australian taxpayers to $2 trillion per year in climate change payments.

factchecks.claim: Solar cycles are driving climate change, not the greenhouse effect.
factchecks.title: Snowball's chance in hell the sun is causing climate change
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Fluctuations in solar activity are far too small to be responsible for recent climate change. Data shows man-made emissions and the greenhouse effect are responsible.
factchecks.explanation: Solar cycles are driving climate change, not the greenhouse effect.

factchecks.claim: Humans are responsible for just three per cent of atmospheric CO2.
factchecks.title: New MP's climate change sums don't add up
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Human activity has contributed to more than a third of carbon dioxide in the earth’s atmosphere.
factchecks.explanation: Humans are responsible for just three per cent of atmospheric CO2.

factchecks.claim: A respected US academic has downplayed the impact of global warming and suggested it may benefit civilisation.
factchecks.title: Selective editing distorts expert's climate change views
factchecks.verdict_label: Misleading. The video is edited to omit a key disclaimer that he was being intentionally contrarian as part of a broader discussion on the dangers of climate change.
factchecks.explanation: A respected US academic has downplayed the impact of global warming and suggested it may benefit civilisation.

factchecks.claim: A graph proves that the rise in atmospheric C02 is dominated by natural factors, not anthropogenic emissions.
factchecks.title: Climate change myth mixes up its maths on CO2 rates
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The graph misleadingly compares the rate at which CO2 is being added each year with the amount that is in the atmosphere.
factchecks.explanation: A graph proves that the rise in atmospheric C02 is dominated by natural factors, not anthropogenic emissions.

factchecks.claim: There has been no net warming in Australia over the past 10 years.
factchecks.title: Climate sceptic's shot at Aussie data misses net warming facts
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Temperatures have increased slightly since 2012 and data over a longer period shows a significant warming trend.
factchecks.explanation: There has been no net warming in Australia over the past 10 years.

factchecks.claim: Human-based carbon dioxide emissions do not cause global warming.
factchecks.title: Sunny outlook on global warming's causes denies scientific evidence
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Human activity is causing climate change due to an increase in greenhouse gases.
factchecks.explanation: Human-based carbon dioxide emissions do not cause global warming.

factchecks.claim: Zali Steggall's climate change bill required emissions targets to be set by an unelected commission, which could override elected officials.
factchecks.title: Near net zero truth in Wilson's climate bill claim
factchecks.verdict_label: Mostly False: MPs would have set the target by voting for the bill. The minister’s decision could only be vetoed if trying to bring the target forward - a measure removed before the bill was tabled in parliament.
factchecks.explanation: Zali Steggall's climate change bill required emissions targets to be set by an unelected commission, which could override elected officials.

factchecks.claim: NSW has the fastest-growing economy in Australia.
factchecks.title: Perrottet wrong on fastest-growing economy claim
factchecks.verdict_label: False. NSW’s economy grew by 1.8 per cent in 2021-22, the lowest growth of all states and territories.
factchecks.explanation: NSW has the fastest-growing economy in Australia.

factchecks.claim: The Australian economy is performing better than that of any other country after COVID-19.
factchecks.title: Minister overstates COVID comparison with 'world's best' economy ...
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Australia has had a strong recovery from the pandemic, but there are several other countries that have performed better on key indicators.
factchecks.explanation: The Australian economy is performing better than that of any other country after COVID-19.

factchecks.claim: Australia spends twice what Taiwan spends on defence, despite the two countries having similar-sized economies.
factchecks.title: Military spend comparison problematic, say experts
factchecks.verdict_label: Mixture. The claim is only true when looking at a specific GDP measure, which experts say is problematic.
factchecks.explanation: Australia spends twice what Taiwan spends on defence, despite the two countries having similar-sized economies.

factchecks.claim: NZ Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern bought Dominion Voting machines for use in elections.
factchecks.title: NZ voting machine claim pushes the wrong buttons
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The prime minister has not purchased the machines and they've never been used in NZ elections.
factchecks.explanation: NZ Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern bought Dominion Voting machines for use in elections.

factchecks.claim: Livestream footage of several locations in the Middle East is evidence the war in Gaza is fake.
factchecks.title: Fake war claim is conspiratorial nonsense
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Gaza is not one of the locations shown on multiple livestream cameras.
factchecks.explanation: Livestream footage of several locations in the Middle East is evidence the war in Gaza is fake.

factchecks.claim: No one “said a word” in opposition to the 2003 US-led Iraq War.
factchecks.title: Iraq War post is a claim of mass deception
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Historical evidence shows widespread global opposition, by governments and citizens, to the 2003 Iraq War.
factchecks.explanation: No one “said a word” in opposition to the 2003 US-led Iraq War.

factchecks.claim: Finland defeated Russia with a single bullet in the Winter War of 1939-40.
factchecks.title: No, Finland didn't win the Winter War with 'a bullet and a prayer'
factchecks.verdict_label: False. There is no evidence, experts say. The war ended with signing of the Moscow Treaty where Finland ceded about 10 per cent of its territory to the Soviet Union.
factchecks.explanation: Finland defeated Russia with a single bullet in the Winter War of 1939-40.

factchecks.claim: 7000 Ukrainian troops invaded Iraq in 2003.
factchecks.title: Post misleads on Ukraine's role in Iraq War
factchecks.verdict_label: Misleading. The Ukraine was not part of the invading force in March 2003. In addition, the most troops the Ukraine had in Iraq at any one time was 1700.
factchecks.explanation: 7000 Ukrainian troops invaded Iraq in 2003.

factchecks.claim: A "physics professor" says a mind-control weapon was used successfully in the Gulf War to force Iraqi troops to surrender.
factchecks.title: There's no evidence mind control led Iraqi troops to surrender in the ...
factchecks.verdict_label: False. There is no evidence such technology was used, or that it exists. In addition, the video's caption incorrectly identifies the speaker as a leading physics professor.
factchecks.explanation: A "physics professor" says a mind-control weapon was used successfully in the Gulf War to force Iraqi troops to surrender.

factchecks.claim: A behind-the-scenes video reveals Palestinians attempting to fake war casualties.
factchecks.title: 'Gaza footage' mislabelled in war fakery claim
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The footage is from the set of a Lebanese short film about Palestine. It does not purport to be real-life footage.
factchecks.explanation: A behind-the-scenes video reveals Palestinians attempting to fake war casualties.

factchecks.claim: A video shows a gun battle between Israel and Hamas in Gaza.
factchecks.title: Iraq War footage rehashed as Gaza conflict
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The footage is from the Iraq War in 2004.
factchecks.explanation: A video shows a gun battle between Israel and Hamas in Gaza.

factchecks.claim: Australia is the only G20 nation that doesn’t use nuclear power.
factchecks.title: Dutton's claim about G20 nuclear energy use doesn't add up
factchecks.verdict_label: Misleading. Five other G20 nations don’t generate nuclear power, and two of those don't use it.
factchecks.explanation: Australia is the only G20 nation that doesn’t use nuclear power.

factchecks.claim: A law will give the UK government the power to fine or even jail people if their homes don’t meet energy efficiency standards.
factchecks.title: Energy jail threat claim fails to ignite
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The UK Energy Act 2023 doesn't empower the government to issue fines or jail people.
factchecks.explanation: A law will give the UK government the power to fine or even jail people if their homes don’t meet energy efficiency standards.

factchecks.claim: Wind turbines must spin continuously for four years to replace the energy it took to manufacture them.
factchecks.title: Wind turbine energy claim is all spin and no power
factchecks.verdict_label: False. It typically takes about six months for turbines to recoup the energy costs of making them.
factchecks.explanation: Wind turbines must spin continuously for four years to replace the energy it took to manufacture them.

factchecks.claim: There are 89 days worth of oil stock in Australia.
factchecks.title: Energy minister misleads on oil reserves in Australia
factchecks.verdict_label: Misleading. At the time of the claim, Australia had 64 days of oil in the country. A further 25 days of stock were in transit or overseas.
factchecks.explanation: There are 89 days worth of oil stock in Australia.

factchecks.claim: $35 billion in renewable energy projects have been rolled out in Australia in the past three years.
factchecks.title: Treasurer exaggerates scale of renewable energy boom
factchecks.verdict_label: False. In the past three years, $24.8 billion has been invested in renewable energy projects, industry analysts say. Annual spending has been declining since 2018.
factchecks.explanation: $35 billion in renewable energy projects have been rolled out in Australia in the past three years.

factchecks.claim: The US government demolished Nikola Tesla’s Wardenclyffe Tower to prevent him giving free energy to the world.
factchecks.title: Tesla free energy meme shockingly short on truth
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Tesla’s plans were for wireless electricity transmission but he was unable to make it commercially viable and the tower was demolished to pay his debts.
factchecks.explanation: The US government demolished Nikola Tesla’s Wardenclyffe Tower to prevent him giving free energy to the world.

factchecks.claim: The federal Labor government sent debt collection letters to 12,000 Queenslanders who couldn’t pay their energy bills.
factchecks.title: Wires crossed on energy debt notices claim
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The Queensland customers were referred to debt collection agencies by energy companies, not the government.
factchecks.explanation: The federal Labor government sent debt collection letters to 12,000 Queenslanders who couldn’t pay their energy bills.

factchecks.claim: Australia is the only OECD country that doesn’t produce nuclear power.
factchecks.title: Barnaby's meltdown over nuclear energy claim
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Eighteen of the 38 OECD countries don't produce nuclear power.
factchecks.explanation: Australia is the only OECD country that doesn’t produce nuclear power.

factchecks.claim: Ukraine and Russia were already at war when Labor made its election promise to reduce electricity bills by $275.
factchecks.title: Dutton muddles Labor's energy promise timeline
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Labor announced the policy on December 3, 2021, almost three months before Russia invaded.
factchecks.explanation: Ukraine and Russia were already at war when Labor made its election promise to reduce electricity bills by $275.

factchecks.claim: A new law regulating gene technology in New Zealand is being passed under “Fast Track legislation” and will “bypass” provisions of the Bill of Rights Act protecting medical choice.
factchecks.title: No, NZ's new gene technology bill won't 'bypass' the Bill of Rights
factchecks.verdict_label: Mostly false. The law was not introduced under “Fast Track legislation” and will not impact the right to decline a medical treatment under the Bill of Rights Act.
factchecks.explanation: A new law regulating gene technology in New Zealand is being passed under “Fast Track legislation” and will “bypass” provisions of the Bill of Rights Act protecting medical choice.

factchecks.claim: Five-year-olds are made to question their gender as part of New Zealand Ministry of Education guidelines.
factchecks.title: No, five-year-olds are not made to question their gender
factchecks.verdict_label: False: The claim is not featured in the guidelines or policy documents. Neither are several other claims made in the post.
factchecks.explanation: Five-year-olds are made to question their gender as part of New Zealand Ministry of Education guidelines.

factchecks.claim: A Victorian government policy strips parents of their rights and coerces children into medical gender transition treatments.
factchecks.title: Medical gender transition claim is simply not true
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The policy relates to non-medical transition and has no impact on the rights of parents when it comes to medical procedures.
factchecks.explanation: A Victorian government policy strips parents of their rights and coerces children into medical gender transition treatments.

factchecks.claim: The coalition government has narrowed the gender pay gap.
factchecks.title: Minister's claim about gender pay gap doesn't pay off
factchecks.verdict_label: Misleading. The gender pay gap narrowed under the coalition but experts say the primary driver was workplace equality laws introduced by Labor in 2012.
factchecks.explanation: The coalition government has narrowed the gender pay gap.

factchecks.claim: Around 38 per cent of the Liberal Party’s federal parliamentarians are women.
factchecks.title: Treasurer jumbles the numbers on Liberal women in parliament
factchecks.verdict_label: Misleading. 38 per cent of the party's senators are women, but its female representation across both houses of parliament is significantly lower.
factchecks.explanation: Around 38 per cent of the Liberal Party’s federal parliamentarians are women.

factchecks.claim: Amnesty International has published posters protesting Israel’s participation in the 2024 Olympics.
factchecks.title: Iran media pushes fake Amnesty posters protesting Israel at Olympics
factchecks.verdict_label: False. Amnesty International says it is not responsible for the posters.
factchecks.explanation: Amnesty International has published posters protesting Israel’s participation in the 2024 Olympics.

factchecks.claim: Proposed laws will allow Queensland authorities to order social media users to remove any content they don't like.
factchecks.title: Bill won't let state govt delete social media posts it doesn't like
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The bill would only allow police to order social media platforms to remove content depicting certain criminal acts, posted for specific purposes.
factchecks.explanation: Proposed laws will allow Queensland authorities to order social media users to remove any content they don't like.

factchecks.claim: An ABC Media Watch segment exposed COVID-19 crisis actors.
factchecks.title: No, ABC Media Watch did not expose COVID-19 crisis actors
factchecks.verdict_label: False. The original Media Watch video debunked claims that NSW Health hired crisis actors.

factchecks.claim: You cannot sleep with your cousin (hanzvadzi) in Africa
factchecks.title: 'Kissing cousins': Cousin marriages in Africa not always taboo
factchecks.verdict_label: False The claim by Chin’ono that ‘You cannot sleep with your cousin (hanzvadzi) in Africa’ is false. Firstly, because not all African cultures consider cousins as siblings. In some cultures like SeSotho, SeTswana and iSiNdebele, cousins are cousins. They  differentiate between parallel cousins (children of a father’s brother or mother’s sister) who are considered sisters/brothers and cross cousins (children of a father’s sister or mother’s brother) who remain cousins. Cross cousin marriages for some of these  communities happen and are legal under Zimbabwe’s laws and other countries, such as Lesotho. However, it remains unclear if ‘an estimated 35% to 50% of all sub-Saharan African populations ‘prefer or accept’ cousin marriages’ as stated by Iqbal Mohamed MP.
factchecks.explanation: You cannot sleep with your cousin (hanzvadzi) in Africa

factchecks.claim: Growth in the mining sector output from US$3-4 billion six years ago to an annual output of US$14 billion.
factchecks.title: Chinamasa Exaggerates Mining Sector Growth
factchecks.verdict_label: The claim that ‘Growth in the mining sector output from US$3-4 billion six years ago to an annual output of US$14 billion’ is false. When the initial target of US$12 billion in the mining sector was set out in 2019, it was for export earnings. Under the US$12 billion mining roadmap, gold was expected to contribute US$4 billion, platinum US$3 billion while chrome, iron, steel diamonds and coal contribution was set at US$1 billion. Lithium was expected to contribute US$500 million while other minerals were targeted at US$1,5 billion. This has not been achieved. Instead, the government changed this target to include US$5,2 billion investment between 2018 and 2023; US$5,4 billion export earnings plus local consumption. So, no, the mining sector annual output has not reached $14 billion as claimed.
factchecks.explanation: Growth in the mining sector output from US$3-4 billion six years ago to an annual output of US$14 billion.

factchecks.claim: 2,500 women die giving birth each year.
factchecks.title: Beyond the Headlines: The Complex Reality of Maternal Mortality
factchecks.verdict_label: The claim that ‘2,500 women die giving birth each year’ has been rated false. The maternal mortality rate has gone down. The latest statistics have 1,589 deaths, not 2,500. The rest of the claim is a bit more complicated. Are women dying as a result of the hospital having only one theatre? Research shows that it is more nuanced than that. While having only one theatre is a challenge in carrying out emergency c-sections, most of the maternal deaths are not as a result of only not having theatres. It’s a combination of also not having enough personnel, blood or drugs. factchecks.claim: However, the overall positive development marks a significant milestone, being the first quarter-on-quarter rise in employment observed since the onset of economic challenges brought about by the Covid-19 pandemic.

The 1st quarter of 2023 recorded 3,207,535 people employed and in the 2nd quarter of 2023 the number was 3,239,965. This marked a quarter on quarter rise. In the 3rd quarter of the same year, the number of individuals employed was recorded by ZimStat as 3,121,007. A drop from the 2nd quarter. It, however, rose again in the 4th quarter of 2023 to 3,173,293 marking a quarter on quarter rise before the current one to 3,289,853, the highest in over a year.
factchecks.explanation: However, the overall positive development marks a significant milestone, being the first quarter-on-quarter rise in employment observed since the onset of economic challenges brought about by the Covid-19 pandemic.

factchecks.claim: Oil and gas are not fossil fuels; they are a renewable energy source created by a geothermal reaction between the solid mantle and liquid core. factchecks.verdict_label: Scientific evidence shows that hydrocarbon deposits on Earth form over geologic time as biological matter is buried in sedimentary basins and undergoes chemical transformations. factchecks.explanation: Oil and gas are not fossil fuels; they are a renewable energy source created by a geothermal reaction between the solid mantle and liquid core. Hydrocarbons are generated in the upper mantle, then transported through deep faults and deposited in Earth’s crust in any rock type and structural position.

factchecks.claim: ‘Only 2% of Zim women own agricultural land: World Bank’
factchecks.title: NewsDay, Not 2% of Zim women but 2% of the documented agricultural population are women
factchecks.verdict_label: The claim that ‘only 2% of Zimbabwean women own agricultural land’ attributed to the World Bank in the NewsDay story has been rated as misleading. It is not what the World Bank says. The World Bank in its report claims, ‘Documented ownership of agricultural land is low in Zimbabwe, just 2 percent of women’. ZimStat, the primary source of the figure says, ‘Overall, 2.8 percent of the agricultural population have documented ownership of the agricultural land with women constituting 2 percent’. The claim is, therefore, rated as misleading since the figures from the survey indicate that, ‘2% of the 2.8% of the agricultural population with documented ownership are women’ not that just 2% of Zimbabwean women own agricultural land. The population being referred to is the agricultural population with documented ownership not the whole of Zimbabwean women.
factchecks.explanation: ‘Only 2% of Zim women own agricultural land: World Bank’

factchecks.claim:
A social media user says there were 56 deaths in ICE custody during the two terms of Democratic US President Barack Obama (2009-1017). The user insinuated the numbers are similar to deaths under Republican Donald Trump and complained about alleged double standards in public perception.

One post on X with 1,1 million views for example, says "OBAMA ERA: 56 DIE IN ICE CUSTODY, AMERICA SAYS WHATEVER. 56 people died in ICE custody under Obama. What happened you may ask? No riots. No cities on fire. No 'Obama is Hitler' banners. Trump does raids and suddenly it's the end of civilization."
factchecks.title: Fact check: Trump vs. Obama on ICE deaths and deportation
factchecks.verdict_label: DW Fact check: Misleading The number of 56 deaths under Obama is not entirely correct. The figure of 56 deaths comes from the 2016 report ACLU/DWN/NIJC report "Fatal Neglect: How ICE Ignores Deaths in Detention". But the report covers only through early 2016, before Obama's final year in office, which ended only at the beginning of 2017. According to a list from ICE, a total of 67 detainees died during Obama's eight years of presidency (2009–2017).  The number of deaths in ICE custody are already higher under Trump, as the infographic below shows. So far, the count is at 83 deaths. Trump's second term shows a particularly sharp rise. ICE counts deaths by fiscal year (October to September), but looking at the first 12 months of Trump's second term, there were 37 deaths.  The number of deaths accumulated in the first year of Trump's second term is comparable to the number of deaths accumulated under Obama in four years.  Immigration law scholar Cesar Cuauhtemoc Garcia Hernandez told DW: "The Trump administration is currently on track to see the largest number of deaths by people who are detained by ICE."  The Ohio State University law professor attributes this to more people being detained and kept for longer periods.  Deaths in detention are separate from deaths involving ICE enforcement actions. In January 2026, two high-profile ICE shootings of US citizens sparked a public outcry and lead to a drop in support for ICE.
factchecks.explanation:
A social media user says there were 56 deaths in ICE custody during the two terms of Democratic US President Barack Obama (2009-1017). The user insinuated the numbers are similar to deaths under Republican Donald Trump and complained about alleged double standards in public perception.

One post on X with 1,1 million views for example, says "OBAMA ERA: 56 DIE IN ICE CUSTODY, AMERICA SAYS WHATEVER. 56 people died in ICE custody under Obama. What happened you may ask? No riots. No cities on fire. No 'Obama is Hitler' banners. Trump does raids and suddenly it's the end of civilization."
